report.headline: Airport halted since 8:10 PM, 290 minutes — no takeoff or landing since XY278 at 8:10 PM; no takeoff since XY277 at 1:39 PM; GACA 12:46 AM: 12 dead, 309 injured; NOTAM A3586/26 still suspends ops through Sunday 2100 UTC; 481 flights cancelled today so far.
report.synopsis: There were 0 takeoffs in the last hour, the latest XY277 to Sharm el-Sheikh at 1:39 PM. The latest landing was XY278 from Sharm el-Sheikh at 8:10 PM, with 0 landings in the last hour. 481 flights are cancelled today (232 departures, 249 arrivals) and 1 arrivals have diverted. Yesterday, 9 October: 166 of 703 flights cancelled, 18 arrivals diverted and four halts of 45+ minutes, the longest 7:41 to 9:38 PM (no landing until 9:45 PM). No official reason has been given for the evening stop. Saturday morning: a 91-minute halt ran from 6:37 to 8:08 AM with no takeoff or landing. Saturday afternoon–evening: the board showed no takeoff or landing from 2:05 PM until flynas XY278 from Sharm el-Sheikh landed at 8:10 PM (~365 minutes). Since that landing there has been no further takeoff or landing — open halt since 8:10 PM (290 minutes at the 1:00 AM Sunday slot). Last takeoff remains flynas XY277 at 1:39 PM; prior last landing before XY278 was Air Cairo SM461 at 2:05 PM. GACA confirms King Khalid International Airport was attacked on Saturday afternoon and operations remain temporarily suspended until damage assessment and facility safety checks are complete. GACA follow-up statement at 12:46 AM Sunday (dated 11 October): the attack resulted in 12 fatalities — 4 Saudi citizens and residents of Bangladeshi (2), American (1), Egyptian (1), Jordanian (1), Syrian (1), Palestinian (1) and Sudanese (1) nationality — and 309 injured, including some in critical condition; property damage is being assessed. AIS/NOTAC shows NOTAM A3586/26 (NOTAMR) keeping the aerodrome unavailable from 10 Oct 19:24 UTC through 11 Oct 21:00 UTC. Flightradar24 at 11:35 PM reported Dammam-bound flights holding (including one originally for Riyadh); at 12:01 AM FR24 said flights were on approach to Dammam again. Reuters at 9:40 PM had restated the suspension with “several” wounded — GACA’s 12:46 AM tally supersedes that on casualties. AP reports an official saying a missile struck a passenger terminal and wounded many; AFP hospital source earlier said dozens injured / at least five Saudis in ICU; AFP diplomatic source said Houthis hit with a missile around 3:00 PM. Social-media death-toll claims circulating earlier remain unverified against the new official GACA figures. No official Houthi claim for Saturday found yet. Passengers told to confirm flight status before heading to the airport. Board cancellations remain elevated on Sunday 11 October.

strikes.title: Escalation pattern: Houthi strikes on KSA by target type
strikes.so_what: The campaign has climbed an escalation ladder: from military targets to economic targets (Aramco, Yanbu), then to symbolic targets (the Madinah power station serving the Prophet’s Mosque), and now to civilian aviation and the capital. King Khalid International Airport has now been hit or targeted on 19 Sep, 5, 7, 8 and 10 Oct; the 10 Oct strike closed it indefinitely, and a projectile fell near Dammam’s airport the same evening. Each rung raises the reputational cost to the Kingdom more than the military cost.

items.title: Houthis claim missile and drone strike on Aramco site in Riyadh
items.detail: Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed ballistic missiles and drones hit an Aramco facility in Riyadh, causing fires; smoke was seen near an Aramco site south of the city.

items.title: Coalition calls Houthi Riyadh claims "misleading"
items.detail: Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said the Houthis were trying to divert attention from their losses.

items.title: Coalition: 97 strikes on Houthi reinforcements in Taiz
items.detail: The coalition said it carried out 97 precise targeting operations on the Tor al-Baha front and Taiz axis.

items.detail: Saudi Arabia said 3 people were injured in attacks on Jazan and Najran airports as fighting with the Houthis reignited.

items.title: Houthis claim strikes on RUH and an Aramco refinery
items.detail: Explosions were heard in Riyadh; the Houthis claimed King Khalid airport and an Aramco refinery as targets.

items.detail: The mutual defence pact was activated after the Houthi attacks.

items.title: Air France, KLM, BA and Cathay Riyadh suspensions in force
items.detail: Air France and KLM suspended Riyadh (KLM also Dammam) to 24 Oct; BA resumes 1 daily flight on 3 Nov; Cathay suspended to 31 Jan 2027.

items.title: UK Embassy security alert; FCDO advice flags airports
items.detail: The UK issued an alert and updated travel advice on 6 Oct, after a US Mission alert on 5 Oct.

items.title: GACA: Abha airport attack, 2 killed, 28 injured
items.detail: Two women, a Moroccan and an Algerian, were killed at Abha International Airport.

items.title: GACA: KKIA attack, 1 killed, 8 injured
items.detail: A Sudanese man was killed at King Khalid airport; RUH traffic halted for over an hour.

items.title: Coalition: missile intercepted north of Riyadh
items.detail: The Houthis claimed a KKIA strike; the coalition said a missile was intercepted north of Riyadh.

items.title: GCC, Arab leaders and UN chief condemn airport attacks
items.detail: GCC and Arab leaders and the UN Secretary-General condemned the deadly attacks on Saudi airports.

items.detail: Interception debris damaged a kindergarten and a medical complex in Riyadh.

items.detail: Claim relayed from Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree.
